```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.model_selection import (train_test_split, RandomizedSearchCV,
                                     StratifiedKFold)
from sklearn.inspection import PartialDependenceDisplay
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, label_binarize
from xgboost import XGBClassifier, XGBRegressor
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, f1_score, confusion_matrix, classification_report,
    roc_auc_score, roc_curve, auc,
    r2_score, mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error
)
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

df = pd.read_csv("data/who_wb_cleaned.csv")
print(f"Raw data: {df.shape[0]} rows, {df['country_code'].nunique()} countries")
```

# Feature Engineering

```{python}
#| label: feature-eng

df["hiv_per1000"] = (df["hiv_new_infections_per1000"] / df["population"]) * 1000
df["malaria_per100k"] = (df["malaria_deaths"] / df["population"]) * 100000

df["log_gdp"] = np.log1p(df["gdp_per_capita_ppp"])

df["tb_ncd_ratio"] = df["tb_incidence_per100k"] / (df["ncd_mortality_pct"] * 100)

df["infectious_burden"] = (df["tb_incidence_per100k"]
                           + df["hiv_per1000"] * 100
                           + df["malaria_per100k"])

df_model = df[df["year"] == 2019].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

feature_cols = [
    "tb_incidence_per100k", "ncd_mortality_pct", "hiv_per1000", "malaria_per100k",
    "gdp_per_capita_ppp", "health_expenditure_pct_gdp", "urban_population_pct",
    "log_gdp", "tb_ncd_ratio", "infectious_burden"
]

X = df_model[feature_cols].copy()
print(f"Modeling dataset: {df_model.shape[0]} countries, {len(feature_cols)} features")
print(f"Features: {feature_cols}")
```

---

# Part 1: XGBoost Classification — Predicting Income Group

We classify each country into one of four World Bank income groups using disease and economic indicators.

## 1.1 Train/Test Split and Baseline Fit

```{python}
#| label: clf-baseline

income_order = ["Low income", "Lower middle income", "Upper middle income", "High income"]
le = LabelEncoder()
le.fit(income_order)

y_clf = le.transform(df_model["income_group"])

X_train_c, X_test_c, y_train_c, y_test_c = train_test_split(
    X, y_clf, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y_clf
)

print(f"Train: {X_train_c.shape[0]} | Test: {X_test_c.shape[0]}")
print(f"Class distribution (train): {dict(zip(income_order, np.bincount(y_train_c)))}")

xgb_base_clf = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=5,
    learning_rate=0.1,
    importance_type="gain",
    eval_metric="mlogloss",
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_base_clf.fit(X_train_c, y_train_c)

y_pred_base_c = xgb_base_clf.predict(X_test_c)
acc_base = accuracy_score(y_test_c, y_pred_base_c)
f1_base = f1_score(y_test_c, y_pred_base_c, average="macro")
print(f"Baseline — Accuracy: {acc_base:.3f} | Macro F1: {f1_base:.3f}")
```

## 1.2 Feature Importance (Baseline)

```{python}
#| label: fig-imp-clf
#| fig-cap: "Feature importance (gain) from the baseline XGBoost classifier."

imp_c = pd.Series(xgb_base_clf.feature_importances_, index=feature_cols)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
imp_c.sort_values().plot.barh(ax=ax, color="#1f77b4")
ax.set_xlabel("Importance (mean gain)")
ax.set_title("Feature Importance — Baseline XGBoost (Classification)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

print("Top 5:", imp_c.nlargest(5))
```

## 1.3 Bias-Variance Tradeoff

```{python}
#| label: fig-bv-clf
#| fig-cap: "Training and test error as a function of boosting rounds."

xgb_bv_clf = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=600, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.1,
    eval_metric="mlogloss", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_bv_clf.fit(X_train_c, y_train_c)

n_rounds = list(range(10, 610, 10))
train_err, test_err = [], []

for n in n_rounds:
    tr_pred = xgb_bv_clf.predict(X_train_c, iteration_range=(0, n))
    te_pred = xgb_bv_clf.predict(X_test_c, iteration_range=(0, n))
    train_err.append(1 - accuracy_score(y_train_c, tr_pred))
    test_err.append(1 - accuracy_score(y_test_c, te_pred))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
ax.plot(n_rounds, train_err, "o-", label="Training Error", markersize=3)
ax.plot(n_rounds, test_err, "s-", label="Test Error", markersize=3)
ax.set_xlabel("n_estimators (boosting rounds)")
ax.set_ylabel("Error Rate (1 − Accuracy)")
ax.set_title("Bias-Variance Tradeoff: Boosting Rounds vs Error (Classification)")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

best_n_c = n_rounds[np.argmin(test_err)]
print(f"Best round: {best_n_c} (test error: {min(test_err):.4f})")
```

## 1.4 Hyperparameter Tuning (RandomizedSearchCV)

XGBoost minimizes a regularized objective with L2 ($\lambda$), L1 ($\alpha$), and tree complexity ($\gamma$) penalties:

$$
\mathcal{L} = \sum_i \ell(y_i, \hat{y}_i) + \sum_k \left[ \gamma T_k + \frac{1}{2}\lambda \lVert w_k \rVert^2 + \alpha \lVert w_k \rVert_1 \right]
$$

```{python}
#| label: clf-tuning

param_dist_clf = {
    "max_depth": [3, 5, 7, 9],
    "learning_rate": [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3],
    "reg_lambda": [0.1, 1, 10],
    "reg_alpha": [0, 0.1, 1],
    "subsample": [0.7, 0.8, 1.0],
}

rand_search_clf = RandomizedSearchCV(
    estimator=XGBClassifier(
        n_estimators=300, eval_metric="mlogloss",
        importance_type="gain", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
    ),
    param_distributions=param_dist_clf,
    n_iter=30,
    cv=StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42),
    scoring="f1_macro",
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1, verbose=1
)
rand_search_clf.fit(X_train_c, y_train_c)

print(f"Best params: {rand_search_clf.best_params_}")
print(f"Best CV Macro F1: {rand_search_clf.best_score_:.3f}")
```

## 1.5 Early Stopping

```{python}
#| label: clf-early-stop

X_tr_c, X_val_c, y_tr_c, y_val_c = train_test_split(
    X_train_c, y_train_c, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train_c
)

xgb_es_clf = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=2000,
    **rand_search_clf.best_params_,
    eval_metric="mlogloss",
    early_stopping_rounds=50,
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_es_clf.fit(X_tr_c, y_tr_c, eval_set=[(X_val_c, y_val_c)], verbose=False)

print(f"Best iteration: {xgb_es_clf.best_iteration}")
print(f"Val log-loss: {xgb_es_clf.best_score:.4f}")
```

## 1.6 Final Tuned Model

```{python}
#| label: clf-final

best_n_est_clf = min(xgb_es_clf.best_iteration + 50, 2000)

xgb_final_clf = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=best_n_est_clf,
    **rand_search_clf.best_params_,
    eval_metric="mlogloss",
    importance_type="gain",
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_final_clf.fit(X_train_c, y_train_c)

y_pred_tuned_c = xgb_final_clf.predict(X_test_c)
acc_tuned = accuracy_score(y_test_c, y_pred_tuned_c)
f1_tuned = f1_score(y_test_c, y_pred_tuned_c, average="macro")

print(f"Tuned — Accuracy: {acc_tuned:.3f} | Macro F1: {f1_tuned:.3f}")
print(f"Improvement over baseline — Accuracy: {acc_tuned - acc_base:+.3f} | F1: {f1_tuned - f1_base:+.3f}")
```

## 1.7 Confusion Matrix

```{python}
#| label: fig-confusion
#| fig-cap: "Confusion matrix for the tuned XGBoost classifier on the test set."

cm = confusion_matrix(y_test_c, y_pred_tuned_c)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5.5))
sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues",
            xticklabels=income_order, yticklabels=income_order, ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("Predicted")
ax.set_ylabel("Actual")
ax.set_title("Confusion Matrix — Tuned XGBoost")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

print(classification_report(y_test_c, y_pred_tuned_c, target_names=income_order))
```

## 1.8 ROC Curves (One-vs-Rest)

```{python}
#| label: fig-roc
#| fig-cap: "ROC curves (one-vs-rest) for all four income groups."

y_test_bin = label_binarize(y_test_c, classes=[0, 1, 2, 3])
y_prob_c = xgb_final_clf.predict_proba(X_test_c)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5.5))
colors = ["#d62728", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c", "#1f77b4"]

for i, (label, color) in enumerate(zip(income_order, colors)):
    fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_test_bin[:, i], y_prob_c[:, i])
    roc_auc_val = auc(fpr, tpr)
    ax.plot(fpr, tpr, color=color, lw=2, label=f"{label} (AUC = {roc_auc_val:.2f})")

ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "k--", lw=1)
ax.set_xlabel("False Positive Rate")
ax.set_ylabel("True Positive Rate")
ax.set_title("ROC Curves (One-vs-Rest) — Tuned XGBoost")
ax.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

macro_auc = roc_auc_score(y_test_bin, y_prob_c, multi_class="ovr", average="macro")
print(f"Macro AUC: {macro_auc:.3f}")
```

## 1.9 Partial Dependence Plots

```{python}
#| label: fig-pdp-clf
#| fig-cap: "Partial dependence plots showing the marginal effect of the top 3 features on predicted income group."

top3_clf = imp_c.nlargest(3).index.tolist()
print(f"Plotting PDP for: {top3_clf}")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 4))
for i, feat in enumerate(top3_clf):
    PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        xgb_final_clf, X_train_c, [feat],
        target=0,
        ax=axes[i], grid_resolution=50
    )
    axes[i].set_title(feat)
fig.suptitle("Partial Dependence — XGBoost Classification (target: Low income)", y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

# Part 2: XGBoost Regression — Predicting Life Expectancy

We predict life expectancy at birth from disease burden and economic indicators.

## 2.1 Train/Test Split and Baseline Fit

```{python}
#| label: reg-baseline

y_reg = df_model["life_expectancy"].copy()

X_train_r, X_test_r, y_train_r, y_test_r = train_test_split(
    X, y_reg, test_size=0.3, random_state=42
)

print(f"Train: {X_train_r.shape[0]} | Test: {X_test_r.shape[0]}")
print(f"Life expectancy range: {y_reg.min():.1f} – {y_reg.max():.1f} years")

xgb_base_reg = XGBRegressor(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=5,
    learning_rate=0.1,
    importance_type="gain",
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_base_reg.fit(X_train_r, y_train_r)

y_pred_base_r = xgb_base_reg.predict(X_test_r)
rmse_base = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test_r, y_pred_base_r))
r2_base = r2_score(y_test_r, y_pred_base_r)
print(f"Baseline — RMSE: {rmse_base:.2f} years | R²: {r2_base:.4f}")
```

## 2.2 Feature Importance (Baseline)

```{python}
#| label: fig-imp-reg
#| fig-cap: "Feature importance (gain) from the baseline XGBoost regressor."

imp_r = pd.Series(xgb_base_reg.feature_importances_, index=feature_cols)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
imp_r.sort_values().plot.barh(ax=ax, color="#2ca02c")
ax.set_xlabel("Importance (mean gain)")
ax.set_title("Feature Importance — Baseline XGBoost (Regression)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

print("Top 5:", imp_r.nlargest(5))
```

## 2.3 Bias-Variance Tradeoff

```{python}
#| label: fig-bv-reg
#| fig-cap: "Training and test RMSE as a function of boosting rounds."

xgb_bv_reg = XGBRegressor(
    n_estimators=600, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.1,
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_bv_reg.fit(X_train_r, y_train_r)

n_rounds = list(range(10, 610, 10))
train_err_r, test_err_r = [], []

for n in n_rounds:
    tr_pred = xgb_bv_reg.predict(X_train_r, iteration_range=(0, n))
    te_pred = xgb_bv_reg.predict(X_test_r, iteration_range=(0, n))
    train_err_r.append(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_train_r, tr_pred)))
    test_err_r.append(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test_r, te_pred)))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
ax.plot(n_rounds, train_err_r, "o-", label="Training RMSE", markersize=3)
ax.plot(n_rounds, test_err_r, "s-", label="Test RMSE", markersize=3)
ax.set_xlabel("n_estimators (boosting rounds)")
ax.set_ylabel("RMSE (years)")
ax.set_title("Bias-Variance Tradeoff: Boosting Rounds vs RMSE (Regression)")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

best_n_r = n_rounds[np.argmin(test_err_r)]
print(f"Best round: {best_n_r} (test RMSE: {min(test_err_r):.3f} years)")
```

## 2.4 Hyperparameter Tuning (RandomizedSearchCV)

```{python}
#| label: reg-tuning

param_dist_reg = {
    "max_depth": [3, 5, 7, 9],
    "learning_rate": [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3],
    "reg_lambda": [0.1, 1, 10],
    "reg_alpha": [0, 0.1, 1],
    "subsample": [0.7, 0.8, 1.0],
}

rand_search_reg = RandomizedSearchCV(
    estimator=XGBRegressor(
        n_estimators=300, importance_type="gain",
        random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
    ),
    param_distributions=param_dist_reg,
    n_iter=30,
    cv=5,
    scoring="neg_root_mean_squared_error",
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1, verbose=1
)
rand_search_reg.fit(X_train_r, y_train_r)

print(f"Best params: {rand_search_reg.best_params_}")
print(f"Best CV RMSE: {-rand_search_reg.best_score_:.2f} years")
```

## 2.5 Early Stopping

```{python}
#| label: reg-early-stop

X_tr_r, X_val_r, y_tr_r, y_val_r = train_test_split(
    X_train_r, y_train_r, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
)

xgb_es_reg = XGBRegressor(
    n_estimators=2000,
    **rand_search_reg.best_params_,
    early_stopping_rounds=50,
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_es_reg.fit(X_tr_r, y_tr_r, eval_set=[(X_val_r, y_val_r)], verbose=False)

print(f"Best iteration: {xgb_es_reg.best_iteration}")
print(f"Val RMSE: {np.sqrt(xgb_es_reg.best_score):.2f} years")
```

## 2.6 Final Tuned Model

```{python}
#| label: reg-final

best_n_est_reg = min(xgb_es_reg.best_iteration + 50, 2000)

xgb_final_reg = XGBRegressor(
    n_estimators=best_n_est_reg,
    **rand_search_reg.best_params_,
    importance_type="gain",
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
xgb_final_reg.fit(X_train_r, y_train_r)

y_pred_tuned_r = xgb_final_reg.predict(X_test_r)
rmse_tuned = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test_r, y_pred_tuned_r))
r2_tuned = r2_score(y_test_r, y_pred_tuned_r)
mae_tuned = mean_absolute_error(y_test_r, y_pred_tuned_r)

print(f"Tuned — RMSE: {rmse_tuned:.2f} years | R²: {r2_tuned:.4f} | MAE: {mae_tuned:.2f} years")
print(f"Improvement in RMSE: {rmse_base - rmse_tuned:.2f} years")
```

## 2.7 Regression Diagnostics

```{python}
#| label: fig-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Left: Predicted vs actual life expectancy with 45° reference line. Right: Residual distribution."

residuals = y_test_r - y_pred_tuned_r

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.5))
axes[0].scatter(y_test_r, y_pred_tuned_r, alpha=0.6, s=30,
                edgecolors="white", linewidth=0.5, c="#2ca02c")
mn, mx = y_test_r.min(), y_test_r.max()
axes[0].plot([mn, mx], [mn, mx], "r--", lw=1.5)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Actual Life Expectancy (years)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Predicted (years)")
axes[0].set_title("Predicted vs Actual")
axes[1].hist(residuals, bins=15, color="#2ca02c", edgecolor="white", alpha=0.8)
axes[1].axvline(0, color="red", linestyle="--", lw=1.5)
axes[1].set_xlabel("Residual (years)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("Count")
axes[1].set_title("Residual Distribution")

plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## 2.8 Partial Dependence Plots

```{python}
#| label: fig-pdp-reg
#| fig-cap: "Partial dependence plots showing the marginal effect of the top 3 features on predicted life expectancy."

top3_reg = imp_r.nlargest(3).index.tolist()
print(f"Plotting PDP for: {top3_reg}")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 4))
PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
    xgb_final_reg, X_train_r, top3_reg,
    ax=ax, grid_resolution=50
)
fig.suptitle("Partial Dependence — XGBoost Regression", y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
